findings.title: UnixFileLock follows a symlink at the lock path and truncates its target (O_TRUNC without O_NOFOLLOW)
findings.evidence: UnixFileLock._acquire() builds open_flags = os.O_RDWR | os.O_TRUNC (line 41) and then calls os.open(self.lock_file, ...) (line 44) with no O_NOFOLLOW and no lstat/symlink rejection. self.lock_file is the caller-supplied lock path (BaseFileLock.__init__, _api.py:184, os.fspath(lock_file)), which is frequently a predictable path in a world-writable directory such as /tmp. If a local attacker plants a symlink at that path pointing at a file the victim can write (e.g. /home/victim/.ssh/config), os.open resolves the link and O_TRUNC empties the target before fcntl.flock is even attempted. This is deterministic, not only a race: Path(self.lock_file).exists() (line 42) follows the link, reports True, so O_CREAT is omitted and the open truncates the link target immediately. Even when the link is swapped in after the exists() check, the check-then-open gap on lines 42-44 is a TOCTOU window (CWE-367) that lets the attacker win. After truncation the victim continues to hold and later fchmod/flock/close the descriptor, so the destructive write happens under the victim's own credentials without any write access to the target being needed. Fixed upstream in filelock 3.20.1 by adding O_NOFOLLOW (CVE-2025-68146 / GHSA-w853-jp5j-5j7f).

findings.title: WindowsFileLock follows a symlink/reparse point at the lock path and truncates its target (O_CREAT|O_TRUNC)
findings.evidence: WindowsFileLock._acquire() computes flags = os.O_RDWR | os.O_CREAT | os.O_TRUNC (lines 22-26) and calls os.open(self.lock_file, flags, ...) (line 28) without verifying that the path is a regular file or rejecting a reparse point (symlink/junction). The preceding guard raise_on_not_writable_file(self.lock_file) (line 20) does not help because it resolves the link target via os.stat (see _util.py:22) and only classifies mode/writability, it never refuses a symlink; the subsequent open resolves the reparse point and truncates the target. A local attacker on Windows (symlink creation requires Developer Mode or the create-symbolic-link privilege; junctions are also usable) who can write the directory containing a predictable lock path can therefore make the victim truncate an arbitrary file it can write. Upstream fixed this by adding a GetFileAttributesW reparse-point check before opening (CVE-2025-68146 / GHSA-w853-jp5j-5j7f).

findings.title: raise_on_not_writable_file inspects a symlink's target via os.stat instead of lstat
findings.evidence: raise_on_not_writable_file() calls os.stat(filename) (line 22), which follows symbolic links, and then bases its PermissionError / IsADirectoryError decision on the link target's st_mode/st_mtime (lines 26-36). This helper gates the WindowsFileLock and SoftFileLock acquire paths (called at _windows.py:20 and _soft.py:17). A hostile symlink planted at the lock path therefore makes the writability pre-check inspect and disclose attributes of an attacker-chosen target file rather than reject the link, and it is the 'check' half of the check-then-open pattern that reaches os.open in _windows.py:28. Upstream changed this to os.lstat and moved the real defense to the open (O_NOFOLLOW / reparse-point check) in the 3.20.1 fix for CVE-2025-68146.
